holidays.name: Mayday Distress Signal Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the international radio distress call, 'Mayday, Mayday, Mayday,' which has nothing to do with spring flowers and everything to do with emergencies at sea and in the air. Celebrate by learning when it is actually appropriate to shout it.
holidays.origin: The call was created in 1923 by Frederick Stanley Mockford, a senior radio officer at Croydon Airport in London. He needed a word that pilots and controllers would understand easily, and since much air traffic ran between Croydon and Paris, he chose 'mayday' from the French 'venez m'aider' meaning 'come help me.'
holidays.funFact: The word is repeated three times so it cannot be mistaken for background noise or a similar-sounding phrase in a garbled transmission.

holidays.name: Save the Rhino Day (Observed Around Now) / National Chocolate Parfait Day
holidays.description: A dessert holiday for the layered, spoon-wielding fancy folks of the world. Chocolate parfait Day invites you to stack chocolate, cream, and crunchy bits in a tall glass and pretend you are dining at a Parisian cafe, even if you are standing at your kitchen counter in socks.
holidays.origin: Like many American food holidays, it grew out of the unofficial calendars compiled by food marketers and enthusiasts. The word parfait is French for 'perfect,' and the dessert originally referred to a frozen custard-like dish.
holidays.funFact: In France, a parfait is a smooth frozen dessert, while the American version with layers of yogurt, fruit, and granola is a relatively modern twist.

holidays.name: Loyalty Day
holidays.description: An official U.S. holiday dedicated to reaffirming loyalty to the United States and recognizing the heritage of American freedom. It is one of the strangest federal observances because most people have never heard of it, yet it has been proclaimed by presidents every year.
holidays.origin: It began as 'Americanization Day' in 1921 and later became 'Loyalty Day' in the 1950s during the Cold War, partly as a counter to the international communist May Day celebrations. Congress made it a permanent annual observance in 1958.
holidays.funFact: Loyalty Day was created largely as a rival to the workers' May Day parades, so May 1 effectively has two competing political holidays in one date.

holidays.name: Space Cowboy Day
holidays.description: A day to saddle up your imaginary rocket and ride the cosmos in the spirit of space cowboys everywhere. Think Western hats, laser pistols, and quoting sci-fi shows about bounty hunters drifting through space.
holidays.origin: It is a pop culture celebration tied to the anime series Cowboy Bebop, which began airing in Japan in 1998. Fans use the day to celebrate the show's jazz soundtrack, bounty hunters, and iconic closing line 'See you, space cowboy.'
holidays.funFact: The Cowboy Bebop soundtrack by Yoko Kanno is so beloved that it helped introduce jazz and blues fusion to a whole generation of anime fans.

holidays.name: Mother Goose Day
holidays.description: A day for nursery rhymes, fairy tales, and generally celebrating the legendary storyteller who gave us Humpty Dumpty, Little Miss Muffet, and Jack and Jill. It is the perfect excuse to recite a rhyme out loud in public and see who joins in.
holidays.origin: The day was created in 1987 by children's author Gloria T. Delamar, who wrote a book on Mother Goose's history. She wanted to encourage parents and teachers to share nursery rhymes with children.
holidays.funFact: No one is certain who Mother Goose really was. Some say she was a real woman in Boston, while others trace the name to French tales published by Charles Perrault in 1697.
